transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-26
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (Heliograph Eng Mgr); Tom Alvarez (Heliograph SRE); Nina Park (DataOps); Liam O'Rourke (CTO, joined briefly)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Align on runtime onboarding steps for Redwood Private deployment into Helio's staging VPC, discuss KMS/keys and SOC2 checklist, schedule benchmark window and share runbook.
- Agreement to run small pilot with 2 models (chat + embeddings) and evaluate latency/cost targets.

Topics:
- VPC connectivity and peering
- KMS/HSM and data retention settings
- Pilot scope and success criteria
- Benchmark timings and tooling

Transcript Body:
00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey folks, thanks for jumping on. I see most of the team here; I'll kick us off. Quick round—Priya, you're with me from the SE side.
00:14 Priya (Redwood SE): Yep hi, Priya Nair. I'll focus on the runtime and infra bits, perf tests.
00:20 Maya (Heliograph): Maya here, hi. We're excited, we had a lot of internal Q's after the kickoff deck—mostly around private / vpc setup and encryption.
00:32 Tom (Heliograph): Tom Alvarez, SRE. We're the ones who actually wire up the VPC peering and the firewall rules, so want to make sure we don't break any compliance gates.
00:44 Jordan: Great. Goal for today — align on the onboarding runbook, verify what's needed for staging VPC, and pick dates for the perf window. We'll capture action items as we go.
00:58 Nina (Heliograph): Nina Park, DataOps. I'll be owning dataset sanitize and sample prompts to share.
01:10 Jordan: Cool. First high-level question: are you planning Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) or a Redwood Dedicated with peered networking? I know from the pre-call notes you said 'private'.
01:28 Maya: Correct, we want Private for data isolation. We're leaning on our Azure VPC, want to ensure keys live in our KMS — we don't want Redwood to hold keys.
01:41 Priya: That's supported — we can integrate customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. Quick note, there are a couple of deployment options: private with customer KMS, or private with customer-managed HSM for extra FIPS boundaries. Which one do you anticipate?
01:58 Tom: We'll likely do Azure Key Vault; we have HSM-backed keys there. Is there any extra latency with KMS calls during inference? We want to keep token-latency < 150ms in staging.
02:15 Priya: KMS calls are only for initial unwrapping during container startup, after that the runtime keeps secrets in memory. So no per-request KMS hop. But if you rotate keys frequently we should coordinate restarts.
02:31 Maya: Good to know. Also curious about log retention and audit logs — we need audit trails for model version and request traces for our SOC-2 audit.
02:44 Jordan: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM, and we expose per-request metadata and traces. We'll include a SOC 2 checklist snippet in the runbook we share.
02:58 Liam (CTO, briefly): Jumping in — what about data residency for embeddings? We can't send raw PII to hosted endpoints.
03:10 Jordan: For Private, data sits in your VPC and we don't persist payloads unless you opt in. We'll detail defaults in the privacy section.
03:24 Priya: For the pilot I suggest two pathways: embeddings inside your VPC with no payload persistence, and a chat model with prefix caching disabled so we can measure cold-latency.
03:40 Tom: That sounds good. What's the minimal infra footprint we need? How many GPUs for the staging pilot?
03:52 Priya: For a small pilot, 2x A40-equivalent nodes should be fine for batch of 10 concurrent low-latency tests; if you want parallelism to simulate 100 qps you would scale to 6 nodes. But let's start small.
04:10 Maya: Our staging budget is limited — can we just do one node and run at reduced QPS to get latency numbers?
04:20 Priya: Yes, single node will give you baseline latency and throughput curves. We'll generate a perf profile and suggest quantization if needed to meet latency targets.
04:34 Jordan: Perf window — propose next Tue (2026-05-04) 09:00 PT for the initial benchmark. Priya, does that work for you?
04:45 Priya: That works; I'll reserve 30 minutes and prep the scripts.
04:50 Maya: Works for our team as well.
05:00 Jordan: Sam's note — we need sample prompt set and the PII policy to configure data-masking. Maya, can you provide that by Friday?
05:12 Maya: Yes, I'll drop it to the shared drive. Expect a zipped prompt set and a short policy doc.
05:20 Tom: On the VPC peering front — we'll need the exact CIDR and a small firewall change request. Can Redwood provide a minimal inbound/outbound port list for ops?
05:34 Priya: Absolutely. We'll send a one-pager with ports (gRPC + health/probes + SSH jump box for support) — and a template CIDR allowance. Note: we'll also support SSM style access if you prefer no open SSH.
05:48 Jordan: I'll add that as an attachment in the runbook link.
06:00 (Speaker 1): There's a quick question on model pinning — can we pin a model version so we don't get unexpected regressions in output quality during the pilot?
06:12 Priya: Yes, you can pin to a specific model commit/variant; Redwood also supports canaries and automatic fallback. We'll show the rollout UI in a follow up demo.
06:26 Nina: For embedding vectors, what's the default storage TTL? We may want shorter retention during pilot.
06:36 Jordan: Default is 30 days in the managed store, but for Private you control persistence. We'll set pilot TTL to 7 days per your request.
06:48 Tom: About costs — what drives cost for dedicated/private? CPU vs GPU? We need a rough estimate for the pilot node.
07:00 Jordan: The unit cost is driven by GPU-hours and model size (memory). We'll provide a cost sheet with expected per-1k token and per-embedding costs for your config.
07:16 Maya: Great. On the security checklist — does Redwood support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning?
07:26 Jordan: Yup, SAML SSO and SCIM are both supported. We'll need IdP metadata and an admin user list to complete provisioning.
07:36 (Noisy background briefly) Tom: Sorry, construction noise — will mute.
07:44 Priya: No worries, audible. One other infra detail: do you plan to run any heavy batch evals that will persist the KV cache? If so we should consider eviction policies.
07:58 Maya: We'll have nightly batch evals but they won't be latency-sensitive. We can keep caching enabled for production but might disable it in staging to measure cold starts.
08:12 Jordan: Noted. I'll put cache toggles in the runbook.
08:22 (Speaker 2): Question — regarding network egress audit, we need to prove no payloads left the VPC. How do we validate that?
08:36 Priya: We can enable egress allow-list and provide packet-level logs, plus the Redwood runtime will show last-hop metadata for every request. We'll coordinate with your SIEM team.
08:52 Tom: Ok. For the benchmark, what's the exact test harness you use? We prefer synthetic traffic but with our prompt templates.
09:04 Priya: We'll use a JMeter + custom harness that replays your prompt set, records p95/p99 latency, token costs, and CPU/GPU utilization. We'll hand off the scripts so you can reproduce.
09:18 Jordan: Also attaching a short bootstrapping checklist: identity, VPC peering, KMS info, node sizing, sample prompts, and contact points.
09:32 Nina: Quick ask — could Redwood redact PII inline before embeddings? We have some fuzzy names in logs.
09:44 Priya: We can enable a pre-tokenization filter to remove phone numbers and emails; for names we recommend a policy-based replace or a custom preprocessor.
09:58 Maya: For compliance we also need retention reports. Does Redwood produce automated retention audit reports?
10:12 Jordan: Yes, report generation is supported — we'll include a sample retention report for the runbook.
10:24 (Interruption) Maya: Sorry, real quick — does Redwood support K8s-based on-prem? We're evaluating an air-gapped option.
10:36 Priya: We have an on-prem package that runs behind your firewall with a customer control plane; air-gapped deploys require a different install cadence and manual package signing. We can discuss in a security deep-dive if you choose that path.
10:54 Jordan: Let's add that as a follow-up security call. I'll propose times.
11:04 (Speaker mislabel: Speaker 3): Liam chimed in earlier — he'll be the exec sponsor; he'll want a 1 pager summarizing SLA and rollback policy.
11:20 Jordan: Absolutely. We'll draft an executive brief with SLAs, escalation path, and rollback plan.
11:32 Priya: Back to perf — couple of gotchas: sequence length matters a lot, if your prompts average 1.2k tokens you'll see different throughput than 256 token prompts. Please include histograms when you provide sample prompts.
11:50 Nina: We'll add token length histograms to the prompt set.
12:00 Tom: Any constraints around tenant isolation if we have multiple teams using the same cluster?
12:12 Priya: We'll set up namespaces, RBAC and per-token billing breakdown. You can have route-level quotas per team.
12:24 Maya: For the pilot success criteria — what should we agree on? I propose: p95 latency < 180ms for chat, embedding p95 < 60ms, and no data egress; also a documented runbook handed to ops.
12:44 Jordan: That sounds reasonable. We'll add those as success criteria in the pilot plan.
12:56 (Background: someone typing) Jordan: Ok, let's recap action items — Maya to share prompt set and policy; Jordan to share runbook and port list; Priya to prep benchmark harness and node sizing; Tom to open firewall request and provide CIDR info.
13:14 Maya: I'll have prompts and policy by Friday.
13:20 Tom: CIDR and firewall ticket by EOD Wednesday.
13:26 Priya: I'll send perf script and reserve May 4th.
13:34 Jordan: I'll upload the onboarding runbook (link will be in calendar invite) and the SOC2 checklist excerpt.
13:42 (Short pause) Nina: One more minor ask — can Redwood's console mask tokens in logs by default? We want to ensure devs don't accidentally see raw inputs.
13:56 Jordan: Yes, token masking is a configurable default. We'll ensure it's enabled for pilot.
14:06 (Wrap) Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook and the calendar invite for the perf window. If any blockers pop up, DM me.
14:18 Maya: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
14:22 Tom: Thanks all.
14:25 Meeting end (approx 48 minutes)

Links/Artifacts referenced:
- Onboarding runbook (will be shared): https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/heliograph-onboard (placeholder)
- Benchmark harness repo (will be shared): https://github.com/redwood/perf-harness (placeholder)
